inputs.rows_used: row_blocks.fixture_observations (18 rows; fields used per row: row_id, a, orientation)

state_reconstructions.marg: rho = diag(cos^2 a, sin^2 a). The L6 incumbent's home object; orientation cannot enter. Included as the family's phase-free control member.
state_reconstructions.hopf_pt(phi0): rho = |psi><psi| with psi = (cos(a) exp(i s phi0), sin(a)), s = orientation. The L7 Hopf-chart representative of the shell at oriented loop position phi = s*phi0. Orientation enters ONLY as the signed loop position, the same way L7's holonomy uses it (traversal direction). phi0 in {pi/5, pi/2}.
state_reconstructions.pair(phi0,dphi): the orientation-ORDERED pair of loop points (pA, pB) = (s*phi0, s*(phi0+dphi)); pB follows pA along the traversal direction. phi0 = pi/5, dphi = pi/7.

basis_index.note: coherence functionals are basis-indexed; the basis is the eigenbasis of n(alpha,beta).sigma with |b_+> = (cos(alpha/2), e^{i beta} sin(alpha/2)), |b_-> = (-e^{-i beta} sin(alpha/2), cos(alpha/2)).
basis_index.structural_note_for_the_record: bz on marg is the incumbent's exact setting. Real-plane bases (beta=0) are invariant under complex conjugation, the antiunitary that implements orientation flip on the Hopf chart; complex-tilted bases are not. Whether that matters is computed, not asserted.

functionals.relent: C_r(rho, b) = S(Delta_b rho) - S(rho), S in bits via a Hermitian eigensolver with eigenvalue clip at 1e-12 (eigensolver mandatory on BOTH terms; closed forms are NOT an admissible leg implementation)
functionals.klasym: F = KL(p||q) - KL(q||p) in bits, where p, q are the populations of Delta_b rho(pA), Delta_b rho(pB) in orientation order, both clipped at 1e-12 then renormalization NOT applied (clip only)
functionals.step: F = func(rho(pB), b) - func(rho(pA), b) for func in {l1, relent}

variant_grid.marg: 2 functionals {l1, relent} x 6 bases = 12 variants, id marg::{func}::{basis}
variant_grid.hopf_pt: 2 phi0 {pi/5, pi/2} x 2 functionals {l1, relent} x 6 bases = 24 variants, id hopf_pt(phi0)::{func}::{basis}
variant_grid.pair_step: 1 pair (pi/5, pi/7) x 2 functionals {l1, relent} x 6 bases = 12 variants, id pair_step(pi/5,pi/7)::{func}::{basis}
variant_grid.pair_klasym: 1 pair (pi/5, pi/7) x 6 bases = 6 variants, id pair_klasym(pi/5,pi/7)::{basis}
